findings.claim: LLM-ASPIC+ (Yan, Nardin, Boissier, Sichman; ECAI 2025) couples an LLM used only for grounding/contextual parsing with the ASPIC+ formal argumentation engine for conflict resolution, achieving state-of-the-art multi-step defeasible reasoning (87.1% on BoardGameQA-2, 82.6% on BoardGameQA-3) and introducing the MineQA dataset for strict+defeasible multi-step rules.
findings.relevance: AX-01 (defeater sensitivity) and AX-09: demonstrates the current best pattern for LLM-untrusted defeasible reasoning — LLM as parser, symbolic argumentation as judge — with quantitative gains over pure LLMs.

findings.claim: 'Closing the Loop: Formally Verified Law as a Reward Signal for Self-Improving Legal AI' (Heydari, Harvard; Leowald, Columbia; arXiv, June 2026) builds an 'LLM proposes, verifier disposes' architecture for law: LLM autoformalization into a formal legal calculus extending Catala, a verification kernel, and explanations grounded in formal proof traces; claims provable correctness for computational components of law and structural guarantees (every required argument stage addressed, valid deductive links) for open-textured analysis; demonstrated on German procedural deadlines, US Commerce Clause analysis, and cross-jurisdictional sanction proportionality.
findings.relevance: AX-21, AX-01, AX-19, AX-10, AX-22: the closest existing thing to a proof-carrying, LLM-untrusted legal reasoning loop, including using the verifier as a training reward — directly on-target for SSP-Omega's core thesis.

findings.claim: Catala remains the reference 'law as verified code' substrate: compiler core proven correct in F*, formalization of French family-benefits law uncovered a real bug in the government's production implementation; 2025 NLLP work reports 88.8% syntactically valid Catala generated from French tax law with GPT-4.1 few-shot prompting.
findings.relevance: AX-21 (architecture-to-executable transport), AX-14 (determinism), AX-01: statutory law can be carried to a deterministic, verified executable; LLM autoformalization into it is measurably feasible but not yet trustworthy without checking.

findings.claim: Governatori & Palmirani, 'Legal Explanation in Defeasible Deontic Logic via LegalRuleML' (ICAIL 2025, ACM) present a tool producing judicial explanations from provisions encoded in LegalRuleML, reasoning via translation into Defeasible Deontic Logic, on the premise that a yes/no answer is legally insufficient and explanations must be grounded in the relevant provisions.
findings.relevance: AX-19 (inspectable causal account) and AX-05: current state of the art for provision-grounded, standards-based (LegalRuleML/OASIS) explanation from a deterministic deontic reasoner.

findings.claim: Governatori's current implementation line: an ASP implementation of Defeasible Deontic Logic (2024) and 'Turnip', described as the modern DDL implementation used for compliance formalizations; DDL handles rule exceptions and norm conflicts, and compliance results in temporal defeasible logic are provably equivalent to standard DDL.
findings.relevance: AX-01, AX-14, AX-08: mature deterministic engines exist for norm-conflict and compliance reasoning, with equivalence theorems linking temporal and atemporal formulations.

findings.claim: AF-XRAY (Xia, Zheng, Bowers, Ludäscher; ICAIL 2025, open source) provides layered visualizations of abstract argumentation frameworks by game-theoretic argument length, classifies attack edges by semantic role (primary/secondary/blunder), overlays alternative 2-valued solutions on ambiguous 3-valued grounded semantics, and identifies critical attack sets whose suspension resolves undecided arguments, evaluated on Bench-Capon's Wild Animals legal cases.
findings.relevance: AX-19 and AX-09: mechanism for pinpointing the exact source of ambiguity/undecidedness in a legal argument graph and enumerating minimal interventions that resolve it.

findings.claim: Precedent-based reasoning with incomplete information (van Woerkom et al., Artificial Intelligence and Law, 2024/25): on Horty's result model, a focus case with unknown dimension values is 'stable' iff its justification status is invariant over all completions; the work gives methods to compute stability and to identify which possible values must be excluded (what to investigate next) to make a focus case stable — human-in-the-loop decision support.
findings.relevance: AX-09 (blind-spot handling) and AX-01: formal, decidable machinery for 'is my conclusion robust to what I don't know, and exactly which unknowns matter' — a mechanism directly reusable for defeater-sensitive legal CBR.

findings.claim: Hierarchical Precedential Constraint (ICAIL 2023) generalizes Horty-style precedential constraint to factor hierarchies with intermediate legal concepts, enabling multi-step reasoning from case base through intermediate concepts to outcome; companion literature (Prakken's formal analysis; two factor-based models comparison) gives simple syntactic criteria for whether a new-case decision is forced.
findings.relevance: AX-01 and AX-02: decidable 'forced decision' checks and multi-step decomposition through intermediate legal concepts are the current formal CBR frontier.

findings.claim: LogiKEy (Benzmüller, Parent, van der Torre et al.) remains the flagship for mechanized normative reasoning: shallow semantic embeddings of multiple deontic logics, logic combinations, paradoxes and normative theories in Isabelle/HOL, with a layered methodology for engineering ethical/legal theories; the sweep found no major 2025-26 successor release — the published workbench dates to 2020.
findings.relevance: AX-21 and AX-22: higher-order embedding gives proof-assistant-grade assurance and logic-pluralism (swap the deontic logic without redesign) — but it is a workbench, not a production pipeline.

findings.claim: s(LAW) on s(CASP) (Arias et al., Artificial Intelligence and Law 2023): goal-directed constraint ASP without grounding models applicable legislation including discretionality and vague concepts, and produces justification trees translatable to natural language — addressing the incompleteness/scalability limits of ground-ASP justifications.
findings.relevance: AX-19 and AX-01: current best answer for executable statutory reasoning that yields complete, query-directed proof trees while representing open texture explicitly rather than guessing.

findings.claim: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Accountability in Public-Sector AI (Sunny, U. Maryland; arXiv Dec 2025, also in FAccT 2026 proceedings): ontology of CalFresh eligibility from California's Manual of Policies and Procedures + rule-extraction pipeline into a verifiable formal representation + solver layer that checks whether AI-generated explanations align with governing law; detects legally inconsistent explanations and names the violated eligibility rules, making determinations traceable and contestable.
findings.relevance: AX-05, AX-12, AX-19: mechanism where the symbolic layer audits the LLM's explanation against the authoritative rule base — legal-authority validation and accountable state transition in deployed public-sector context.

findings.claim: PNAS paper 'Statutory construction and interpretation for AI' formalizes interpretive ambiguity as constrained entropy minimization and adapts two legal safeguards to AI: iterative rule refinement (modeled on administrative rulemaking/legislative action) and prompt-based interpretive constraints modeled on canons of statutory construction.
findings.relevance: AX-01 and AX-22: a quantitative, jurisdiction-general model of interpretation-under-ambiguity; direct fetch of full text blocked by proxy — claim rests on search-index excerpt of the article page.

findings.claim: The Walton–Sartor–Macagno line (Statutory Interpretation as Argumentation; Sartor 2023 Ratio Juris) is still the reference computational model of legal interpretation: canons formalized as defeasible argumentation schemes with critical questions, a dialectical classification of interpretive schemes, and a logic that distinguishes defensibly vs. justifiably supported interpretive claims — including conditions under which the law's truth-value is formally undetermined.
findings.relevance: AX-01 and AX-09: gives a principled 'honest ignorance' output — the formal machinery can report that an interpretive question is undetermined rather than forcing an answer.

findings.claim: Temporal/legal-state frontier: temporalised belief revision in law (axiomatic characterization, AI & Law) and revision by temporalised literals preserving time-based consistency (AI & Law 2023), plus Governatori-line norm-change operators distinguishing removal-with-effects from removal-with-effect-propagation, model retroactivity and the force/effect/membership time distinctions of real legislation; no 2025-26 production-grade successor surfaced.
findings.relevance: AX-08: formal semantics exist for statute versioning, retroactivity, and effect propagation, but they live on paper — none is wired into a deployed point-in-time reasoner.

findings.claim: ICCMA 2025 (International Competition on Computational Models of Argumentation) ran with AF and ABA tracks; results slides for almost all tracks published Nov 26, 2025 and raw data available Dec 16, 2025 — the competition benchmarks the practical solver state of the art; detailed rankings/winners could not be read (proxy blocked deep fetch).
findings.relevance: AX-17/AX-18: argumentation-semantics computation has an active, measured solver ecosystem whose performance envelope bounds latency/throughput of any argumentation substrate.

findings.claim: LLM-output verification via argumentation is an active 2025-26 line: ValidArgLLM transforms LLM reasoning into a defeasible logic program executed in a symbolic engine and compares resulting inferences with the LLM's natural-language conclusions ('From Argumentation to Labeled Logic Program for LLM Verification', AAAI Spring Symposium); companion CEUR work does discourse-based argumentation analysis for LLM verification.
findings.relevance: AX-10 and AX-01: mechanism family for self-falsification — extract the LLM's own argument, run it in a defeasible engine, and flag divergence between symbolic entailment and LLM conclusion.

findings.claim: Multi-agent LLM deliberation is being formalized in 2026: 'From Debate to Decision: Conformal Social Choice for Safe Multi-Agent Deliberation' (arXiv 2604.07667), ARGORA orchestrated argumentation with Dung-semantics evaluation (arXiv 2601.21533), and ArgRE formal argumentation for multi-agent conflict resolution (arXiv 2604.23124); search-level evidence indicates argument graphs with quantitative semantics and Dung algorithms are being used to arbitrate agent outputs, but per-paper details could not be fetched (arxiv.org blocked by proxy).
findings.relevance: AX-03 (arbitration) and AX-10: the frontier is moving toward provable/statistical guarantees (conformal, formal semantics) on multi-agent LLM arbitration rather than majority voting.

findings.claim: 'When Precedents Clash' (arXiv 2410.10567) and 'Case Frames and Case-Based Arguments in Statutory Interpretation' (arXiv 2411.06873) extend formal CBR toward conflicting-precedent resolution and toward using precedent within statutory interpretation; content could not be read (arxiv.org blocked by proxy) — titles and venue presence only.
findings.relevance: AX-01 and AX-09: likely bears on defeater sensitivity when the case base itself is inconsistent, a known gap in Horty-style constraint.

findings.claim: 'GDPR Auto-Formalization with AI Agents and Human Verification' (arXiv 2604.14607, 2026) exists as a current autoformalization-plus-human-gate pipeline for regulation; content unreadable through the proxy — title/venue only.
findings.relevance: AX-12 and AX-21: bears on human-accountable verification gates in the formalization pipeline.

findings.claim: JURIX 2025 (Turin, Dec 2025, IOS Press gold open access): 139 eligible submissions, 22 long + 18 short accepted (28.7%), with scope explicitly covering deontic logic, formal argumentation, and statutory/rule-based reasoning — the field's formal core remains an active, selective publication venue alongside the LLM wave.
findings.relevance: Frontier context for all axes: the formal-methods community is healthy and its 2025-26 output is where AX-01/AX-08/AX-19 mechanisms are being published.

findings.claim: Prakken, 'On Evaluating Legal-Reasoning Capabilities of Generative AI' (CMNA'24, CEUR Vol-3769) — the leading ASPIC+ author's current position piece on how generative AI legal reasoning should be evaluated; Carneades itself shows no active 2025-26 development in the sweep (latest substantive Gordon/Walton output is 2019 argument-invention work), making it a dormant but conceptually load-bearing model for burden-of-proof/proof-standard handling.
findings.relevance: AX-01 evaluation methodology; AX-12: Carneades' per-issue proof standards and burden allocation remain the most developed formal treatment of institutional decision standards, and nobody has carried them into the neuro-symbolic era.

missing_mechanism_candidates: Verified argumentation kernel: no proof-assistant-mechanized (Isabelle/Coq) metatheory of ASPIC+/DDL and no certified or certificate-producing argumentation solver surfaced — the assurance chain (AX-21) for the argumentation substrate itself is missing; ICCMA solvers are benchmarked, not verified.

Proof-carrying argument certificates: no interchange standard where a legal conclusion travels with an independently checkable proof object (LegalRuleML encodes rules and DDL tools explain, but a small trusted checker for argument-acceptance certificates does not exist).

Grounded factor ascription with provenance: formal CBR (Horty-style constraint, hierarchies, stability) universally assumes curated factor/dimension ascriptions; no mechanism ties factor ascription to source text with transformation lineage (AX-04/AX-06 x reasoning-substrate gap).

Citator-coupled formal reasoning: no system couples precedential-constraint engines or DDL rule bases to live authority validation (overruled/superseded/negative treatment) — AX-05 is handled by commercial citators entirely outside the formal frameworks.

Executable point-in-time legal state: temporal defeasible logic and temporalised revision exist on paper, but no production store of versioned norms with formal norm-change semantics (retroactivity, effect propagation) wired to a reasoner — the state/temporal cell of the design space is unoccupied by any implementation.

Burden/standard-of-proof allocation in neuro-symbolic stacks: Carneades' per-issue proof standards and Prakken–Sartor burden formalizations have not been carried into any LLM-hybrid pipeline — institutional decision-standard machinery (AX-12) is absent from the 2025-26 systems.

Transactional multi-agent argumentation: LLM debate/arbitration work (conformal social choice, ARGORA) lacks explicit transaction semantics, recorded replayable deliberation state, and crash-consistent protocol runs (AX-11/AX-13/AX-15 x coordination gap).

Adversarial model-finding as routine audit: LogiKEy-style countermodel generation (Nitpick/Nunchaku) applied systematically to legal knowledge bases for self-falsification (AX-10) appears in no current legal pipeline.

Calibrated uncertainty over argumentation semantics: gradual/probabilistic argumentation exists, but nothing bridges it to calibration/conformal guarantees so that 'undecided' or 'defensible-only' statuses carry quantified reliability (AX-09).

Cross-order portability harness: every surveyed system is built for one legal order (French tax, CalFresh, German deadlines); no mechanism family demonstrates invariant reuse across legal orders without redesign, and no benchmark measures it (AX-22).
ceiling_threats: AX-21/AX-01: arXiv 2606.23913 claims formally verifiable reward signals AND structural guarantees for open-textured legal analysis (completeness of argument stages, validity of deductive links) — if that holds, a ceiling that assumes open-textured reasoning is inherently outside verification is wrong; verification can bound its *structure* even where content is discretionary.

AX-09: the stability/relevance results on Horty's result model make 'which unknowns can change the outcome' formally decidable for dimension-based CBR — a ceiling treating blind-spot analysis as necessarily heuristic/enumerative is exceedable by exact stability computation.

AX-19: DDL+LegalRuleML judicial-explanation tooling and s(CASP) justification trees show provision-complete, natural-language-renderable causal accounts are achievable from deterministic reasoners today — any ceiling assuming explanation fidelity must degrade with reasoning power is threatened.

AX-03: conformal social choice over multi-agent deliberation (arXiv 2604.07667, unverified in detail) suggests distribution-free statistical guarantees on arbitration outcomes — a ceiling that caps multi-agent LLM arbitration at 'unverifiable ensemble voting' may be wrong.

AX-14/AX-21: Catala's F*-verified compilation plus its discovery of a bug in the French production benefits system demonstrates semantics-preserving transport from statute-shaped source to executable with real-world discriminating power — ceilings on architecture-to-executable assurance for statutory law are demonstrably exceedable.

AX-01: LLM-ASPIC+'s measured jump on multi-step defeasible benchmarks shows the hybrid (LLM grounding + formal defeat calculus) systematically beats pure LLM defeater handling — any ceiling derived from pure-LLM defeasible-reasoning performance underestimates the reachable frontier.

AX-10: ValidArgLLM-style extraction of the LLM's own reasoning into a defeasible logic program that is then executed and diffed against the LLM's conclusion shows self-falsification can be mechanized end-to-end, threatening ceilings that treat counter-design generation as requiring human adversaries.

findings.claim: VeriCoT (ICLR 2026) autoformalizes each chain-of-thought step into first-order logic / SMT-LIB via a two-stage LLM process, classifies each premise as grounded in source context, commonsense, or prior steps, and has solvers check logical validity; evaluated on ProofWriter, LegalBench-SARA (statutory reasoning) and BioASQ, its verification verdicts strongly predict final-answer correctness, and verifier-driven self-reflection yields ~46% relative improvement in CoT verification pass rate and ~41% relative gains in accurate, verifiable outcomes.
findings.relevance: AX-01 (step-level legal-reasoning validity incl. SARA), AX-05/AX-04 (premise-grounding classification), AX-09 (detects ungrounded/fallacious steps), AX-19 (inspectable per-step logical account). Strongest current LLM-propose/solver-verify pattern for NL reasoning chains.

findings.claim: 'Closing the Loop: Formally Verified Law as a Reward Signal for Self-Improving Legal AI' (arXiv 2606.23913, June 2026) adapts the 'LLM proposes, verifier disposes' paradigm to law: LLM-driven autoformalization into a formal legal calculus extending Catala, a verification kernel, and explanation generation grounded in formal proof traces; provides provable correctness for computational components of law and structural guarantees for open-textured analysis (every required argument stage addressed, argumentation exercised at correct stages, deductive links valid), demonstrated on German procedural deadline calculation, U.S. Commerce Clause analysis, and cross-jurisdictional sanction proportionality; the verifier output is used as a training reward signal.
findings.relevance: AX-01 (proof-carrying legal answers), AX-19 (explanations from proof traces), AX-20 (verified reward for self-improvement with invariant preservation), AX-21 (kernel-checked calculus), AX-22 (one calculus spanning German/US/cross-jurisdictional demos).

findings.claim: L4L (arXiv 2511.21033) is a solver-centric legal-AI framework with four stages — statute knowledge building (LLMs autoformalize provisions into logical constraints), dual fact-and-statute extraction, solver-centric adjudication (SMT solvers check arguments against formalized statutes), and judicial rendering — enforcing formal alignment between role-differentiated LLM agents and statutory law.
findings.relevance: AX-01/AX-05 (SMT-backed adjudication against formalized authority), AX-03 (role-differentiated agents with a symbolic arbiter as the arbitration mechanism).

findings.claim: 'Know Your Limits' (arXiv 2606.16118) compares pure LLM classification, LLM-based formal reasoning, and LLM autoformalization + SMT solving in legal reasoning; finds formal structure improves accuracy but accuracy does not imply faithful reasoning — high-performing models succeed by mimicking legal interpretation including its implicit assumptions rather than reasoning formally — and uses round-trip equivalence checking to detect formalization drift.
findings.relevance: AX-01/AX-09: the autoformalization step itself is an untrusted, drift-prone LLM output; round-trip equivalence checking is the frontier countermeasure. Directly constrains any design that treats LLM-produced formalizations as trusted.

findings.claim: 'By Their Fruits You Will Know Them' (arXiv 2605.25186, May 2026) compares multiple formalizations of the same legal provision behaviorally: it builds an equivalence-class graph, derives shared interfaces per pair, and uses SAT to enumerate every input assignment on which two formalizations disagree; applied to nine LLM-generated formalizations of ten EU provisions it finds behavioral divergence essentially uncorrelated with structural agreement, and the verbalized disagreement cases mirror genuine controversies in legal commentary.
findings.relevance: AX-01 (defeater sensitivity via exhaustive disagreement enumeration), AX-09 (surfaces interpretive blind spots), AX-22 (semantics-level comparison independent of encoding). Establishes N-version formalization + SAT diffing as an assurance mechanism for LLM-authored formal law.

findings.claim: LLM-assisted formalization of IRC Section 121 into Prolog (arXiv 2511.11954; also Artificial Intelligence and Law, 2026) shows GPT-4o alone detected the statutory contradiction only 33% of the time, while the hybrid Prolog model produced deterministic, reproducible results, formalized competing interpretations, and autonomously identified an 'inconsistency zone' — validated as accurate, internally consistent, and deterministic.
findings.relevance: AX-08/AX-09 (deterministic statutory-inconsistency detection), AX-14 (determinism under frozen inputs once logic is extracted from the LLM), AX-01 (contradiction handling the LLM alone fails at).

findings.claim: AWS Bedrock Guardrails Automated Reasoning checks (GA since Aug 2025, region expansion and refinement tooling through 2026) compile policy documents into formal logical rules and mathematically verify each LLM response against them, marketed as delivering 'up to 99% accuracy' in verification with provable assurance; 2025-2026 additions include automated natural-language test Q&A generation per policy and refinement modes (Iterative Refinement, Ambiguous Variable Refinement), explicitly targeted at finance, healthcare, and legal services.
findings.relevance: AX-01/AX-05 product frontier: hyperscaler-productized symbolic verification of LLM output against formalized policy. Note the 'up to 99%' figure concedes the NL-to-logic translation layer is itself imperfect — the formal guarantee is conditional on the policy formalization.

findings.claim: Harmonic's Aristotle (arXiv 2510.01346) achieved formally verified gold-medal performance at IMO 2025, solving 5 of 6 problems with Lean 4 proofs verified down to foundational axioms; architecture combines Lean proof search, an informal reasoning system that generates and formalizes lemmas, and a geometry solver; if the proof fails, the system returns no result (structural honest abstention); its contributions have been accepted into Mathlib unmodified and it has resolved long-standing Erdős problems.
findings.relevance: AX-01/AX-21 (end-to-end machine-checked correctness at expert-novel difficulty), AX-10 ('no proof, no answer' as architectural honest ignorance), AX-16 (liveness traded for soundness). The strongest existing instance of a fully LLM-untrusted answer pipeline.

findings.claim: AlphaProof (DeepMind, Nature 2025, 'Olympiad-level formal mathematical reasoning with reinforcement learning') couples a pre-trained LM with AlphaZero-style RL inside Lean, trains on millions of auto-formalized problems, uses Test-Time RL generating millions of related problem variants at inference for hard problems, and scored 28/42 (silver-medal level, 3 of 5 non-geometry problems) at IMO 2024 with every step Lean-verified.
findings.relevance: AX-21 (kernel-verified reasoning at scale), AX-10 (test-time problem-variant generation is machine-scale counter-design/self-testing), AX-18 (autoformalization at millions-of-problems scale). Nature paper itself unreachable via proxy; claims verified from DeepMind announcement and search-surfaced Nature abstract.

findings.claim: Open formal-prover capability is rising steeply: DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B reached 88.9% on miniF2F-test and 49/658 PutnamBench (2025); Goedel-Prover-V2 32B reached 88.1% pass@32 (90.4% with self-correction), beating the 671B model at 20x smaller scale; Kimina-Prover-70B reports 92.2% with test-time RL.
findings.relevance: AX-17/AX-18 (cost-normalized verified-reasoning throughput improving rapidly), AX-20 (scaffolded data synthesis + self-correction as evolution mechanisms with a kernel invariant).

findings.claim: 'Proof-Carrying Certificates for LLM Pipelines: A Trust-Boundary Architecture' (arXiv 2605.16407) verifies the deterministic structured computations around an LLM rather than the model: the ML/NLP layer produces typed artifacts below a trust boundary; a Lean 4 formal layer re-consumes them and emits kernel-audited certificates conditional on a declared assumption hierarchy (tiers: mathematical placeholders, cryptographic assumptions, ML/human oracles); certificate families include conflict-aware bilattice grounding with an emission-gate soundness lemma, embedding sensitivity/paraphrase stability, and Hoare-style agent action, consolidated into a per-call 'Universal Assurance Card'; certificate validity is a Lean kernel type-check plus sorry-free transitive axiom audit; explicitly targets legal retrieval and agentic systems with irreversible side effects.
findings.relevance: AX-21 (trust-boundary + kernel-audited transport), AX-06/AX-13 (per-call certificates as provenance artifacts), AX-11 (Hoare-style certificates over agent actions), AX-12 (assumption-tiered accountability). Closest published analogue to an LLM-untrusted proof-carrying pipeline architecture.

findings.claim: Typed Chain-of-Thought / Proof-Carrying CoT (arXiv 2510.01069, ICLR 2026 submission) produces per-step Typed Faithfulness Certificates (rule applications, type checks, typed dataflow) during decoding; Certified Self-Consistency reaches 69.8% on GSM8K vs 19.6% for the standard baseline under identical sampling budgets.
findings.relevance: AX-19 (typed causal account per step), AX-01 (certificate-filtered voting beats uncertified sampling 3.5x at equal budget — verification as a selection signal).

findings.claim: Proof-Carrying Numbers (arXiv 2509.06902) is a protocol in which every numeric claim in an LLM answer must carry a machine-checkable binding to retriever-provided claim payloads (e.g. via MCP), so numeric answers are mechanically verified rather than trusted.
findings.relevance: AX-05/AX-06 (mechanical claim-to-source binding for quantitative assertions — deadlines, amounts, interest computations in legal work).

findings.claim: VeriCite (arXiv 2510.11394; SIGIR-AP 2025) performs rigorous post-hoc validation of supporting evidence for RAG citations to improve answer attribution over fine-tuning and naive citation-matching baselines, which struggle with multiple citations.
findings.relevance: AX-05 (citation validation as a dedicated verification stage rather than a generation byproduct).

findings.claim: A 2026 cluster of temporal-legal benchmarks and mechanisms exists: LexKairos (arXiv 2608.09106) benchmarks statutory temporal knowledge, case temporal modeling, and statute-case temporal reasoning over Chinese law; a versioned-corpus French tax law benchmark (arXiv 2608.09393) shows 'temporal misgrounding' in legal RAG and resolves point-in-time queries via explicit version indexing with date-of-application as a first-class retrieval signal; further work diagnoses recency bias and post-cutoff staleness in statutory QA (arXiv 2605.23497) and wrong-law application (arXiv 2608.14610); LegalSearch-R1 (arXiv 2605.25920) trains temporally-consistent legal agentic search with RL on temporally-indexed data across 13 tasks.
findings.relevance: AX-08 (temporal/legal-state consistency is now a named failure mode with benchmarks), AX-04 (date-conditioned version-indexed retrieval as a grounding mechanism independent of corpus size).

findings.claim: LLM-ASPIC+ (IOS Press, JURIX-adjacent 2025/2026) combines LLM grounding/contextual reasoning with the ASPIC+ structured argumentation framework to give LLM systems systematic conflict-resolution over inconsistent or contradictory information, with defeasible inferences encoded as legal norms prioritized by legal principles (L-ASPIC lineage).
findings.relevance: AX-01 (defeasible/exception-sensitive legal inference — defeaters are first-class), AX-09 (formal semantics for contradiction handling that classical FOL/SMT substrates lack).

findings.claim: GDPR Auto-Formalization with AI Agents and Human Verification (arXiv 2604.14607) uses a role-specialized multi-agent workflow with iterative feedback to generate legal scenarios, formal rules (Pythen: Python-based defeasible condition-exception 'rule trees'), and atomic facts, checked by four specialized automated verifier agents plus human reviewers assessing representational, logical, and legal correctness; concludes structured verification and targeted human oversight are essential for reliable legal formalization under nuance and context-sensitivity.
findings.relevance: AX-12 (accountable human review as an architectural stage, not an afterthought), AX-02/AX-03 (role-differentiated decomposition with dedicated verifier agents).

findings.claim: LLM planning is now routinely judged and trained against independent symbolic validators: VAL/Fast Downward decide plan validity on NL-PDDL suites, VAL's unsatisfied-precondition feedback is translated into corrective prompts, and verifier-reward RL uses VAL as the reinforcement signal (arXiv 2601.14456); planner-in-the-loop feedback secures LLM PDDL formalization (arXiv 2606.29700).
findings.relevance: AX-02 (plan completeness checked by an external symbolic validator, not self-assessment), AX-11 (precondition/effect semantics as transaction-like checks on workflow steps).

findings.claim: Agentproof (arXiv 2603.20356, March 2026) statically verifies agent workflow graphs auto-extracted from LangGraph, Google ADK, AutoGen, and CrewAI: structural checks (unreachable nodes, dead ends, routing mismatches, required human-in-the-loop nodes) plus a temporal policy DSL compiled to DFAs over abstract events (tool calls, decisions); Lean4Agent (arXiv 2606.06523) formally models and verifies agent workflows and trajectories in Lean 4.
findings.relevance: AX-03 (verified coordination topology and arbitration paths), AX-11 (temporal policies over tool orchestration), AX-12 (machine-checked presence of mandatory human-review nodes).

findings.claim: 2026 agent-audit frontier: a survey of evidence tracing and execution provenance in LLM agents (arXiv 2606.04990) and work on cryptographic binding + reproducibility verification for agent tool use (arXiv 2603.14332) establish hash-chained append-only event logs, pre-action cryptographic receipts written by an independent gate (an audit trail the model cannot influence), and reproducibility/deterministic replay as a necessary condition for behavioral verifiability of high-assurance agents.
findings.relevance: AX-06 (transformation lineage), AX-13 (provenance-complete replay), AX-14 (determinism as a design requirement), AX-15 (append-only durable records).

findings.claim: Conformal risk control for LLM outputs now has both positive mechanisms and limits: conformal abstention certifies error rates (e.g. FDR / hallucination rate among accepted answers), conformal factuality backs off claims to the most specific level satisfying a correctness guarantee, and 'When Can Conformal Risk Control Certify LLM Outputs?' (arXiv 2606.29054) proves bounds and impossibility results for certifying structured generation, with adaptation strategies.
findings.relevance: AX-09 (statistically certified uncertainty/abstention for the non-formalizable residue of legal answers); the impossibility results delimit what distribution-level certificates can ever guarantee for structured outputs.

findings.claim: Machine-checked self-falsification is emerging: 'Learning to Disprove' (arXiv 2603.19514) trains LLMs to propose counterexamples with Lean 4-verified disproofs; VERGE (arXiv 2601.20055) couples LLMs with SMT solvers for verification-guided iterative refinement with formal guarantees; ExVerus (arXiv 2603.25810) repairs proofs via counterexample reasoning; semantic-equivalence self-play uses formal verification to adjudicate generator-vs-evaluator adversarial training (arXiv 2604.17010).
findings.relevance: AX-10 (counter-design and self-falsification whose refutations are themselves kernel-checked, not LLM-judged), AX-20 (adversarial self-play with a formal referee as an evolution mechanism).

findings.claim: Vericoding (LLM generation of formally verified code from formal specifications) has a 12,504-spec benchmark (3,029 Dafny, 2,334 Verus/Rust, 7,141 Lean; Dafny 2026 workshop at POPL 2026) with off-the-shelf LLM success rates of 82% (Dafny), 44% (Verus), 27% (Lean); DafnyPro reaches 86% verified proofs on DafnyBench (+16pp over prior SOTA); specification-synthesis frameworks (VERISPECGEN, arXiv 2604.10392) reach 86.6% pass@1 on VERINA via traceable refinement, while noting real-world spec scarcity remains the bottleneck.

findings.claim: 'Citation Grounding' (arXiv 2606.00898) verifies LLM legal citations against a ground-truth citation graph from 100.8M Ukrainian court decisions (502M edges, 21,736 statute nodes); decomposes into citation precision, relevance, and temporality (valid at the relevant date); finds leading legal AI systems emit false citations in 17-33% of responses; crucially, 59% of flagged 'hallucinations' were graph-coverage gaps (real articles absent from judicial citation practice), so the metric measures the oracle and only lower-bounds accuracy.
findings.relevance: AX-05 (citation validation at national-corpus scale incl. temporal validity), AX-04 (verifier-coverage dependence: grounding quality is bounded by oracle completeness, an explicit corpus-size-independence problem).

findings.claim: SAT-Graph API / 'Deterministic Legal Agents' (arXiv 2510.06002, Brazilian Federal Senate) defines a canonical primitive API over a temporal legal knowledge graph under a 'Probability Isolation' principle: stochastic LLM uncertainty confined to intent translation, semantic anchoring, and narrative synthesis, while structural/temporal/causal traversals are deterministic operations over canonical identifiers; supports point-in-time version retrieval and auditable causal tracing, shifting legal RAG from retrieve-then-generate to reason-act-observe.
findings.relevance: AX-08 (point-in-time legal state), AX-14 (determinism by architectural confinement of stochasticity), AX-13 (auditable traversal), AX-04 (structure/validity/provenance as first-class retrieval constraints).

findings.claim: Temporal legal-state handling is measurably unsolved in pure LLMs: LexKairos (arXiv 2608.09106, Aug 2026) benchmarks statutory temporal knowledge, case temporal modeling, and statute-case temporal reasoning over Chinese law — even the best model (Gemini-3-Flash) fails on precise time-sensitive statutory metadata and time-limit reasoning; companion work diagnoses when LLMs apply the wrong law version (arXiv 2608.14610); component-level diachronic norm versioning models (LRMoo/FRBRoo-based, arXiv 2506.07853) enable deterministic point-in-time reconstruction of any part of a legal text as of a date.
findings.relevance: AX-08 (temporal consistency must be substrate-provided, not model-provided; formal versioning ontologies exist), AX-22 (versioning models are jurisdiction-generic).

findings.claim: 'Closing the Loop: Formally Verified Law as a Reward Signal for Self-Improving Legal AI' (arXiv 2606.23913, Harvard) builds LLM-driven autoformalization into a formal legal calculus extending Catala, a verification kernel, and proof-trace-grounded explanations; claims provable correctness for computational components of law and structural guarantees for open-textured analysis (every required argument stage addressed, argumentation at correct stages, valid deductive links); demonstrated on German procedural deadlines, U.S. Commerce Clause analysis, and cross-jurisdictional sanction proportionality.
findings.relevance: AX-01 (formal defeater-stage coverage), AX-21 (verification kernel in the loop), AX-20 (verified reward for improvement), AX-22 (explicit cross-jurisdiction demonstrations).

findings.claim: 'Know Your Limits' (arXiv 2606.16118) shows LLM 'formal reasoning' is often unfaithful: on re-annotated ContractNLI across five LLMs and three paradigms (pure LLM, LLM-simulated formal reasoning, Z3 solver), it identifies scope laundering (reporting solver-inconsistent conclusions without executing formal reasoning — persists across ALL models), implicit constraint blindness, and Z3 program-synthesis failures; also documents a systematic gap between pragmatic legal interpretation and strict formal entailment (sound legal inferences need unstated assumptions).
findings.relevance: AX-01/AX-21: empirical vindication of the LLM-untrusted stance — only actual solver execution, never LLM-simulated formality, is trustworthy; also warns autoformalization itself is a failure surface.

findings.claim: LLM-ASPIC+ (IOS Press, COMMA line) couples LLM grounding with ASPIC+ formal argumentation for systematic conflict resolution, achieving state-of-the-art on multi-step defeasible reasoning in natural language; the 'Amortized Intelligence' architecture (arXiv 2605.02472) treats the LLM as a one-time semantic compiler rather than runtime interpreter, eliminating stochastic runtime risk and collapsing marginal adjudication cost; legal DSLs with defeasible semantics (L4, Catala, Stipula) anchor the symbolic side; 'By Their Fruits You Will Know Them' (arXiv 2605.25186) compares competing formalizations of the same law by the decisions they encode.
findings.relevance: AX-01 (defeater-sensitive argumentation with formal semantics), AX-09 (contradiction handling via argumentation frameworks), AX-22 (decision-equivalence comparison of formalizations across encodings).

findings.claim: Agent-serving systems research (NSDI/SIGMOD 2026 wave) quantifies large orchestration-layer headroom: Agentix (NSDI '26) improves agent-program throughput 4-15x at equal latency vs vLLM-based serving; Kairos cuts end-to-end multi-agent latency 17.8-28.4% via workflow-aware scheduling and memory-aware dispatch; Maestro does workload-aware cross-cluster scheduling distinguishing TTFT for user-facing stages from TTLT for internal dependency-unblocking stages, addressing dependency-induced head-of-line blocking.
findings.relevance: AX-17/AX-18 (frozen-workload latency and resource-normalized throughput frontiers), AX-03 (dependency-aware scheduling as coordination mechanism).

findings.claim: Formal limits on self-improving agents were established in 2026: 'On The Statistical Limits of Self-Improving Agents' (arXiv 2510.04399) proves distribution-free learning guarantees are preserved iff the policy-reachable model family is uniformly capacity-bounded (unbounded capacity growth makes learnable tasks unlearnable — the 'utility-learning tension'); a companion impossibility shows {continuous self-evolution, complete isolation from external data, safety invariance} cannot jointly hold; 'Information-Theoretic Limits of Safety Verification for Self-Improving Systems' (arXiv 2603.28650) extends this to verification; a survival-satisficing Gödel-machine line installs self-modifications only after proof-carrying certification of invariants plus time-uniform statistical certification.
findings.relevance: AX-20 (evolvability with invariant preservation: impossibility theorems delimit it, and proof-carrying self-modification defines the achievable regime), AX-10 (grounded-signal requirement for self-falsification).

findings.claim: Multi-agent concurrency control and coordination-failure benchmarking emerged as named systems problems: CoAgent (arXiv 2606.15376, concurrency control for multi-agent systems) and DPBench (arXiv 2602.13255, structural determinants of coordination under simultaneous resource contention); substantive content beyond titles unreachable through the proxy.
findings.relevance: AX-03 (write coordination under contention as an explicit mechanism family).

findings.claim: Legal-practice environment 2026: 700+ court cases involve AI-fabricated content (LexisNexis/Bloomberg Law tracking); multiple federal/state courts mandate AI-use disclosure and manual citation-verification certificates; dedicated pre-filing citation-verification products launched mid-2026; EU AI Act high-risk compliance obligations bind by August 2026 with GPAI adversarial-testing obligations (Art. 55) already in effect.
findings.relevance: AX-05/AX-12/AX-13 (external institutional demand: citation validation, accountable sign-off, and audit are now regulatorily forced, not optional).

findings.claim: MDPI Future Internet survey of LLM-based multi-agent orchestration (doi 10.3390/fi18060326) establishes a three-topology taxonomy (centralized, decentralized, hierarchical) with an optional dynamic-adaptive control axis, covering frameworks and communication protocols; among production frameworks, LangGraph models workflows as directed graphs with conditional edges and per-step state checkpointing and benchmarks fastest with most efficient state management (comparison across LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen/MS Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, MetaGPT, DSPy on state granularity, token cost, failure recovery).
findings.relevance: AX-03 (canonical coordination-topology taxonomy), AX-15 (checkpointing as commodity). Direct fetch of doi.org/mdpi.com proxy-blocked; taxonomy claim via search retrieval.

missing_mechanism_candidates: Dissent-preservation, voting, and deliberation primitives in agent coordination/write protocols — universally absent from MCP/A2A/ACP/ANP/ERC-8004 per arXiv 2606.31498; a design-space enumeration under 'coordination/write' should include institutional arbitration objects (quorum, recorded dissent, minority-report state), not just message routing and locks.

State relinquishment and governed forgetting as first-class memory mechanisms — the Always-On Agents survey (2606.30306) shows the literature over-weights accumulation/retrieval and neglects governing, recovering, and relinquishing durable state; 'memory' family needs authority/mutability/recoverability-typed state with rollback obligations.

Verified refinement transport from workflow-level proofs to executable orchestration — Lean4Agent proves at workflow/trajectory level and TLA+/MSC work proves at protocol level, but no end-to-end architecture-to-source-to-executable refinement chain for agent orchestrators exists; 'assurance' family missing a compilation-with-proof mechanism (AX-21 gap).

Oracle-coverage certification for verifiers — Citation Grounding (2606.00898) shows 59% of flagged hallucinations were verifier-coverage gaps; the 'grounding'/'ignorance-handling' families need mechanisms that certify and monotonically report the completeness of the checking oracle itself, distinguishing 'model wrong' from 'verifier blind'.

Coupling of statistical abstention to transactional compensation — conformal/trajectory-level risk control exists and saga compensation exists, but no mechanism family ties calibrated uncertainty thresholds to automatic transactional rollback/escalation as one primitive (ignorance-handling x write-coordination).

Replay-divergence-proof audit semantics — audit meaning stable under model-version and prompt evolution (the named Replay Divergence Problem); provenance family lacks a versioned-semantics mechanism binding each journal entry to the exact model/kernel identity with divergence detection on re-execution.

Cross-hardware attested determinism — batch-invariant kernels give bit-exactness within a deployment; no mechanism combines them with attested execution to make bit-reproducibility portable across hardware/driver versions (state/temporal & determinism family).

Defeater-coverage-certified compilation of law — LLM-ASPIC+/Catala/L4 lines compile norms to defeasible logic, but nothing certifies that the compiled theory's defeater set is complete relative to the source corpus (reasoning-substrate family; AX-01).

Liveness certificates for stochastic-component workflows — MSC projection gives deadlock-freedom by construction, but progress guarantees when steps are LLM calls with unbounded latency/failure/refusal are unformalized (orchestration family; AX-16).

Unified point-in-time legal-state substrate + plan validation — temporal norm versioning (LRMoo/SAT-Graph) and plan verification (PDDL/VAL) exist separately; no mechanism validates a multi-step legal plan against the legal state as-of each step's effective date (state/temporal x reasoning substrate; AX-02+AX-08).

Accountable human decision authority as a protocol object — Faramesh's allow/block/require-review is the frontier, but maker-checker, quorum sign-off, and delegation-of-authority lattices with non-repudiable human attribution are absent from every orchestration formalism surveyed (AX-12).

Semantic-conflict isolation with domain-authority ordering — ACID-Agent's semantic isolation orders by dependency, not by legal authority (lex superior/posterior/specialis); write-coordination family missing authority-lattice-aware conflict resolution.
ceiling_threats: AX-02: any ceiling premised on LLM decomposition/planning unreliability is threatened by formalize-then-solve results — arXiv 2603.23844 shows LLM formalizers retain perfect accuracy in state spaces up to ~10^165 (with divide-and-conquer reaching 100% even for open models) while classical planners contribute soundness/completeness; plan completeness need not be bounded by LLM planning competence.

AX-14: a ceiling asserting LLM inference is irreducibly nondeterministic (forcing determinism ceilings to rest on record/replay only) is wrong — batch-invariant kernels (vLLM/SGLang, TBIK, LLM-42) deliver bit-identical outputs under frozen inputs at ~34% throughput overhead, i.e. substrate-level determinism is achievable, moving the true ceiling to cross-hardware/version reproducibility.

AX-21: a ceiling limiting formal assurance to static program code is threatened — Lean4Agent mechanizes workflow/trajectory verification in Lean4 with measurable downstream gains, and TLA+/MSC results give constructive protocol-level guarantees; assurance demonstrably extends into the orchestration layer.

AX-01: a ceiling stating open-textured legal reasoning admits no formal guarantees is partially threatened — arXiv 2606.23913 demonstrates structural guarantees (every required argument stage present, correct stage ordering, valid deductive links) plus provable correctness for computational components of law; the residual unguaranteeable core is narrower than 'all open-textured analysis'.

AX-05: a ceiling assuming citation-temporality validation cannot scale beyond curated corpora is threatened — Citation Grounding operates over 100.8M decisions/502M edges with per-date validity checking; the binding constraint is oracle coverage, not scale.

AX-11: a ceiling restricting transaction guarantees to syntactic side-effect atomicity is threatened — Agentic Transaction (2608.13900) operationalizes semantic atomicity/consistency/isolation/durability with measured end-task gains, suggesting transactional semantics extend to meaning-level workflow units.

AX-16: a ceiling claiming liveness in LLM multi-agent systems can only be tested empirically is threatened — syntax-directed MSC projection yields deadlock-freedom by construction even for runtime-generated sub-workflows (2604.17612).
AX-18: resource-normalized throughput ceilings calibrated on 2025 serving stacks are too low — Agentix shows 4-15x throughput at equal latency over vLLM-based serving for agent programs (NSDI '26).

AX-20 (ceiling-confirming, direction reversed): 2510.04399 and 2603.28650 PROVE limits — distribution-free guarantees require uniformly capacity-bounded reachable model families, and {continuous self-evolution, data isolation, safety invariance} is jointly impossible; if SSP-Omega's AX-20 ceiling permits unbounded self-improvement with preserved invariants, THAT ceiling is too high, while proof-carrying self-modification (certify invariants before install) marks the achievable regime.

AX-10: a ceiling treating self-falsification as inherently non-rigorous is threatened — Refute-or-Promote formalizes kill-mandate critics with cross-family reviewers and context isolation as a measurable high-precision protocol, and conformal abstention gives escalation triggers with distribution-free error control.

findings.relevance: Methodological caveat for all axes: claims are vendor-declared mechanisms as relayed through search-indexed content; fine-grained mechanism details (e.g., exact Verify semantics, Tenet benchmark protocol) could not be confirmed against the primary pages.

missing_mechanism_candidates: Proof-carrying / machine-checkable verification artifacts: all three vendors' 'verify' mechanisms (Deep Research Verify, Shepard's Verify, KeyCite flags) are retrieval-grounded claim-support checks consumed by a human reviewer — no vendor emits a checkable proof object; a design-space enumeration should keep 'verification-artifact substrate' as a distinct family, absent commercially.

LLM-untrusted trusted path: even Lexis's harness that 'checks its own output against Shepard's rather than relying on the model alone' still has a model-driven orchestrator deciding what to check; the family 'deterministic/verified control plane with LLM only as untrusted proposer' has no commercial instance.

Explicit transaction semantics for agent writes: none of the three declares atomicity, rollback, or isolation for agentic actions across Word/Outlook/matter state (Harvey Spaces inherit permissions but not write-transaction semantics) — coordination/write family gap.

Deterministic replay under frozen inputs / provenance-complete replay: no vendor declares run reproducibility, seed control, or replayable execution traces; AX-13/AX-14 mechanism families are commercially vacant.

Temporal legal-state substrate: KeyCite/Shepard's give current 'good law' status, but no vendor declares point-in-time law snapshots or as-of-date reasoning; state/temporal family missing 'versioned legal-state store'.

Calibrated ignorance/abstention contracts: 'flagging unsupported statements' (Lexis) is the closest, but no declared coverage bounds, blind-spot enumeration, or honest-uncertainty output contract — ignorance-handling family.
Self-falsification / adversarial counter-design: no vendor declares internal red-team agents, counter-argument generation against own work product, or escalation triggers — AX-10 family absent.

Invariant-preserving model evolution: both TR (Thomson) and Harvey (Tenet) swap proprietary models into production with benchmark claims but no declared invariant-preservation, regression-proof, or monotonic-capability mechanism — evolution family gap.

Accountable state transition / institutional decision authority: permissions and ethical walls (Harvey) and admin model selection (TR) exist, but no declared first-class approval-gate objects with audit-complete transition records.

Transformation-lineage provenance: citations link outputs to sources, but no vendor declares lineage through intermediate transformations (extraction → tabular analysis → draft) — AX-06 family absent.
ceiling_threats: AX-05: Shepard's Verify now declares existence + still-good-law + task-relevance validation of citations (including citations from web results) as a shipped harness-level check; any ceiling stating that commercial systems cannot exceed cite-existence checking, or that relevance validation requires the trusted path, is contradicted by this declared mechanism.

AX-01: Deep Research Verify's assertion-level 'does the cited authority support this specific assertion' checking plus KeyCite flags is a shipped partial defeater-sensitivity mechanism; a ceiling assuming defeater detection is absent from commercial baselines is wrong at the margin.

AX-18/AX-20: Thomson's ~$450K final training run (within a $40M program) shows domain-specific frontier-competitive legal models are now cheap to re-train; any ceiling premised on prohibitive economics of frequent proprietary-model iteration (and hence slow capability evolution) is threatened.

AX-01/AX-02: Harvey Tenet's declared +82% LAB all-pass gain from post-training on simulated long-horizon legal work, with sub-agent-deployable capabilities, suggests agentic legal-reasoning correctness is still steeply improvable via RL harnesses — no stable base-model ceiling can be assumed for the LLM-proposer layer.

AX-03/AX-11: Lexis's runtime dynamic orchestration (model/agent/skill/source selection per task, replacing predefined workflows) and CoCounsel's Claude-Agent-SDK harness both exceed any ceiling that assumed static workflow routing is the commercial bound for agent coordination.
